INTRO.text: Every year, the Local Government Unit of Polangui and the Sangguniang Bayan pass ordinances that shape daily life for citizens and local businesses.
To make those laws instantly searchable in plain language, we built OrdiSearch—a vector search-based ordinance and policy retrieval system for Polangui.
Let us introduce our team from Bicol University Polangui. I am Kirby Cope, Researcher.
Joining me is Arnel Hapin, Researcher from Bicol University Polangui.
And James Nebria, Researcher from Bicol University Polangui—working with the LGU of Polangui to modernize access to local legislation.

PROBLEM.text: Right now, finding a specific rule in Polangui means opening and scrolling through dozens of long, scanned PDF ordinances by hand.
People know what they want to ask—like 'Are businesses allowed to operate after midnight?' or 'What is the fine for littering?'—but they do not know the exact legal title.
Because ordinances use formal terms like 'permitted commercial operating hours and nighttime trade restrictions,' basic keyword search returns zero matches.
OrdiSearch bridges that gap using dense vector embeddings and hybrid BM25 search—matching the meaning of a question directly to the enacted section.

SIGNIFICANCE_OBJECTIVES.text: We are building this with the Office of the Secretary to the Sangguniang Bayan of Polangui—cutting hours of manual PDF searching down to seconds.
For LGU officials and municipal lawmakers, OrdiSearch provides a fast reference tool to check existing policies and spot overlapping ordinances before drafting new laws.
And for Polangui's citizens, business owners, and policy researchers, it makes local rules on permits, sanitation, and public order clear and accessible.
To achieve this, Objective One identifies the document, metadata, and query requirements of the Sangguniang Bayan of Polangui.
Objective Two designs and builds the system—splitting ordinances into sections, generating vector embeddings, and linking every answer to the source PDF.
And Objective Three evaluates retrieval accuracy, speed, and software quality through controlled retrieval benchmarks and the ISO/IEC 25010 standard.

METHODOLOGY.text: We used Rapid Application Development—moving fast from Requirements Planning with SB Polangui into iterative User Design, Rapid Construction, and Cutover.
When an ordinance PDF is uploaded, PyMuPDF extracts digital text while Tesseract OCR handles scanned pages. A rule-based parser then splits titles, articles, and sections.
Each section chunk is embedded into 384-dimensional vectors using FastEmbed BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 and stored in our Convex database with vector and full-text search indexes.
Users and evaluators can compare four retrieval modes side by side: Keyword BM25, Semantic Vector, Hybrid, and Hybrid + Rerank.

Under the hood, our Three-Tier Architecture connects Next.js 15 and Python FastAPI to our Convex database—storing documents, sections, 384-d vector chunks, and audit logs while preserving official PDFs.

WALKTHROUGH.text: Let us look at the actual OrdiSearch interface. On the landing page, users see the Polangui seal, live corpus counters, and common citizen inquiry cards.
Let us select a real citizen question: 'What are the penalties for illegal waste dumping and littering?' using Hybrid + Rerank mode and click Search Ordinances.
In milliseconds, OrdiSearch returns a Source-Grounded Synthesis with clickable citation badges [1] and [2], plus the ranked ordinance provisions below.
Clicking Citation [1] opens the Parsed Section Inspector sheet on the right—showing the exact extracted claim, retrieval scores, and the highlighted section text.
In the Document Repository tab, staff and citizens can also filter approved Polangui ordinances by title, year, type, or jurisdiction.
Switching to the Admin Portal, the Sangguniang Bayan custodian manages active ordinances, OCR review queues, indexed sections, and background processing jobs.
And in the Admin Evaluation tab, custodians run controlled benchmark experiments across Keyword, Vector, Hybrid, and Hybrid + Rerank directly inside the app.

EVALUATION.text: For our Chapter 3 evaluation methodology, administrators test the system using a human-judged benchmark query set graded against official Polangui ordinance sections.
The built-in Experiment Runner automatically computes Precision@K, Recall@K, MRR, nDCG@K, citation correctness, and median and P95 response latency.
Alongside retrieval metrics, our Admin Quality Survey module collects 5-point Likert ratings across all eight ISO/IEC 25010 software quality characteristics.

CONCLUSION.text: OrdiSearch turns static PDF archives into an instant, source-traceable legal assistant for the Sangguniang Bayan, LGU officials, and citizens of Polangui.
From Kirby Cope, Arnel Hapin, and James Nebria of Bicol University Polangui—thank you for watching our pitch for OrdiSearch!
